articles.title: Recognising wear in curtain tracks and gliders
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for recognising wear in curtain tracks and gliders.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming track, gliders, end stops as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Look for runners that snag, missing end stops or a track that visibly sags while the curtains are at rest.
Do not pull hard against a jammed curtain or work from an unstable chair. Avoid touching brackets fixed high above reach.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Record the room, track type and which section catches; a short photograph taken from floor level may clarify the problem.
Keep the curtain undisturbed if its fixings appear loose. A falling rail or heavy curtain can injure someone.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Check the maker's model information for compatible replacement gliders and end stops.
Arrange appropriate assistance for overhead work or suspect wall fixings; never assume a cosmetic-looking fault is safe.

articles.title: Observing drawer runner wear without dismantling furniture
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for observing drawer runner wear without dismantling furniture.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming front gap, runner, cabinet as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Notice whether a drawer moves unevenly during normal use, rubs its frame or no longer closes flush.
Do not force a stuck drawer or pull it completely out unless the furniture instructions explicitly permit it; heavy drawers can tip.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Note the drawer location, its approximate contents and whether the problem changes when it is lightly loaded.
If the furniture rocks or several drawers open together, stop using it until stability has been assessed.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Keep any manufacturer identification and installation documents with the maintenance record.
For damaged slides, loose cabinet anchors or suspected tipping, arrange a suitable repair rather than improvising hardware.

articles.title: Checking removable bath mats for loss of grip
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for checking removable bath mats for loss of grip.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming edges, backing, surface as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Observe whether a removable mat lies flat and whether its backing has cracked, curled or become visibly worn.
Do not deliberately test traction by stepping on a wet mat. A mat that moves during ordinary use is not reliable.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Check whether the mat suits the actual floor or bath surface according to its product instructions.
Record persistent curling or slipping, and keep the affected area clear while considering a suitable replacement.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Clean and dry the mat only in accordance with the care label, without mixing cleaning products.
Replace mats with degraded backing rather than adding makeshift adhesive that could leave residue or create new hazards.

articles.title: Inspecting a garden hose reel from ground level
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for inspecting a garden hose reel from ground level.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming frame, hose, handle as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Identify the reel type and observe whether its frame stands evenly, its handle is intact and its hose is visibly kinked.
Do not pull against a jammed reel or reach into moving winding parts. Avoid using a hose near electrical equipment.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Record cracked plastic, loose-looking mounting points or hose abrasion without removing any fixed brackets.
If the reel is wall mounted and appears insecure, keep people away from the area beneath it and seek appropriate help.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Store the hose according to the manufacturer's guidance, allowing for local frost and weather exposure.
Keep connector and reel model details together so replacements can be matched without guesswork.

articles.title: Recording window-blind control condition and child-safety concerns
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for recording window-blind control condition and child-safety concerns.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Identify whether the blind has a cord, looped chain or cordless control and note any missing or damaged safety components.
Loose loops and accessible cords can pose a serious strangulation hazard to children. Keep children away and seek competent advice promptly.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Record the blind location, manufacturer if known and whether the control or restraint is damaged, without testing its strength.
Do not improvise cord knots, attachments or tensioning arrangements; suitability depends on the particular blind system.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Check the original installation and product information for the intended safety components.
Arrange prompt professional or manufacturer guidance where controls are damaged or safety arrangements are uncertain.

articles.title: Recognising visible changes around a basin overflow opening
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for recognising visible changes around a basin overflow opening.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming opening, trim, nearby seal as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Locate the overflow opening, if fitted, and observe from the basin side whether its trim is loose or its surface visibly discoloured.
An overflow is not a guarantee against flooding. Do not deliberately fill a basin to test it or put tools into the opening.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Record odours, staining or recurring dampness nearby, distinguishing what was seen from assumptions about the cause.
If water escapes outside the basin or there is evidence of leakage, stop the affected use and contact the responsible person.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Keep the basin model or property maintenance contact in a household record.
Arrange an appropriate plumbing assessment for suspected internal blockage or leaks; do not dismantle concealed fittings.

articles.title: Recording wardrobe door hinge movement and alignment
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for recording wardrobe door hinge movement and alignment.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming door gap, hinge, cabinet as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Notice whether a wardrobe door closes unevenly, rubs its neighbour or has visibly damaged hinge cups.
Avoid leaning on a loose door or opening several heavy doors simultaneously on unstable furniture.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Note which door and hinge is affected and whether the cabinet itself appears level or wobbly.
A wardrobe that rocks, leans or has loose wall restraints needs stability assessment before continued use.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Retain the maker's assembly guide and hardware identifiers if available.
Use suitable professional assistance for damaged fixings or heavy doors rather than attempting an unsupported adjustment.

articles.title: Checking entrance doormats for curled edges and movement
articles.summary: A practical non-invasive household condition check and record for checking entrance doormats for curled edges and movement.

visual.alt: Three-part offline schematic naming corners, backing, route as separate observation areas; it does not depict repair, loading or hazardous testing.
visual.caption: Identify visible condition and record concerns; not a repair instruction.

sections.title: Recognise the condition
paragraphs: Look for lifted corners, fraying, uneven backing and a mat that shifts during ordinary foot traffic.
Do not place a loose mat across an accessible route, fire exit or door swing where it may obstruct movement.

sections.title: Record what is visible
paragraphs: Record whether the mat is indoors or outdoors, the underlying surface and where it moves.
Remove or isolate an obvious trip hazard when safe, keeping the entrance usable for others.

sections.title: Choose a suitable follow-up
paragraphs: Check the intended surface compatibility and care instructions before selecting a replacement.
Reassess after rain or routine cleaning because moisture and debris can change how a mat sits.
